### B2 — SFCC-270, copy-first override

#### Step 2.1 — Copy-first, then STOP

**Changes.** Copy all eight base files verbatim to their mirrored paths, convert each to `.tsx`, update imports, add a `console.log('[overrides] <filename>')` marker to each.

Sources:
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/{index,bonus-product-quantity,product-quantity-picker}.jsx`
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/{index,item-image,item-name,item-attributes,item-price}.jsx`

Do **not** copy the base `.test.js`/`.test.jsx` or `data.mock.js` — we write our own.

**Pass criteria.**
1. All eight files exist at their mirrored `overrides/` paths with `.tsx` extensions. Zero `.jsx` under `overrides/`.
2. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
3. **Zero functional diff.** `git diff --no-index` between each base `.jsx` and its converted `.tsx`, ignoring type annotations, import-path rewrites and the marker line, shows no logic change. The defaults-then-spread order in `item-image`, `item-attributes` and `item-price` is untouched at this step. The `item-name` bug fix is **step 2.2**, not here.
4. `product-item/index.tsx`'s internal imports of `item-variant/*` are rewritten to **relative paths** (`'../item-variant/item-image'`), not the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path. This is the interception rule from `overrideStyling.md` — the base path builds and runs correctly in the app but silently renders the **unstyled base** in Storybook and Vitest, because `.storybook/main.js` aliases the package straight to `node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it. Get this wrong and every story and test in B3 will be exercising base SFCC, not our override, and look fine doing it.

The `shared/ui` barrel trap applies — do not attempt to override individual `shared/ui/<Name>` members; 208 base files import the barrel.
6. **STOP.** Present the eight files to Marcel. Confirm in the running app that each marker logs — including from the wishlist page and a checkout summary, not just the cart — before any functional change. Then remove the markers.

**Skill.** `/override-component`, if it exists in `.claude/skills/`; otherwise the copy-first rule in AGENTS.md directly.

#### Step 2.2 — Restyle to Figma + the `item-name` fix

**Changes.** Co-located recipes `product-item/product-item.css.ts` (exporting `ZimmCartItem`) and `item-variant/item-variant.css.ts` (exporting `ZimmCartItemVariant`). Replace `layerStyle="cardBordered"` and the Chakra array-shorthand geometry (`width={['88px','136px']}`, `display={['none','block',...]}`) with recipe parts and explicit media queries.

Figma values (§11.2): root gap 28px desktop / 24px mobile, align `center` desktop / `start` mobile; image group 132×198 desktop `object-cover` / 67×100 mobile `object-contain`, aspect 288/432, bg `ivory[200]`, `mix-blend-multiply`; Item Details gap 12px desktop / 24px mobile; Item Info column desktop / row-space-between mobile. Colour + size as **one combined string** ("Lilac Sand, One size"), 200px wide, `text.secondary` — SFCC-270's separate colour AC and size AC are **two ACs describing one element**, so do not build two nodes.

The regular-weight 12px caption (Figma `Default/Caption`) has no textStyle — gate finding #13. Use `textStyle="caption"` and override `fontWeight` to regular **in the recipe**, annotated. Do not add a textStyle to `foundation/typography.ts`; that is Tier 1 from a cart ticket.

Two load-bearing requirements from the decision record:
- **Keep defaults-then-spread.** `<Box width={zimmDefault} {...props}>`, never the reverse. `order-summary` calls `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />` and must keep winning.
- **Fix `item-name`.** Base is `<Link {...props} color="black.600">` — spread before the colour, so no caller can ever override it. Move the spread after. No base caller passes `color`, so nothing changes for them.

Make the stepper slot and the actions slot **optional** on the override's render path — the digital gift-card variant has neither (§11.2). Physical gift cards render as a standard 198 item.

2. `item-variant/index.test.tsx` asserts a caller-passed `width` on `CartItemVariantImage` **wins** over the Zimmermann default, and the same for `mr`. This is the regression that breaks `order-summary` if the spread order flips.
3. A test asserts `CartItemVariantName` accepts and applies a caller-passed `color` — proving the base bug is fixed and provable, not asserted.
4. Rendering `product-item` with no stepper and no actions produces neither in the DOM and throws nothing (gift-card API requirement).
5. `recipeGuards.test.ts` passes: recipe keys are `ZimmCartItem` / `ZimmCartItemVariant` (`Zimm*`-namespaced, so they cannot deep-merge with a base recipe), and no bare Chakra token key appears on a registered scale.
6. `recipeParts.test.ts` passes for both recipes.
7. `npm run audit:tokens` reports no new raw hex/px/rem/em in `product-item/` or `item-variant/`.

### B3 — SFCC-795 + 271, states and stepper

#### Step 3.1 — `ZimmQuantityStepper` molecule

**Changes.** New molecule composing two `ZimmButton`s at `size="icon"` around a value display. Gap **8px (`xs`)** per §11.11(1) — design showed a 12px gap around a 12px glyph with no touch target; we apply the system's 24px `minW`/`minH` (ZimmButton `icon` already is `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`), which adds 6px invisible padding each side, so 8px yields 14px apparent. Annotate exactly that, citing WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 and the Figma node literally named `touchTarget` at 24.

Disabled glyphs use `OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED = 0.4` from `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/zimmCartItemShared.ts` — Figma ships separate greyed SVGs; we use opacity. One constant, one file, read by both the recipe and the tests.

**Pass criteria — every state named, because a state absent here is absent from the Tester's brief and the Scorer's gate:**
1. Quantity 1: `−` is `disabled`, carries `aria-disabled` or the native attribute, renders at 0.4 opacity; clicking it does nothing and quantity stays 1 (AC3).
2. Quantity > 1: both enabled; `−` decrements by exactly 1; `+` increments by exactly 1 (ACs 1, 2).
3. Quantity at max: `+` disabled and greyed, `−` still enabled (795 stepper group).
4. Fully OOS or unavailable: **both** disabled and greyed (795 stepper group).
5. **Hover, focus-visible and active** are inherited from `ZimmButton`'s `icon` variant, which already carries `_hover`/`_focusVisible`/`_active`/`_disabled`. Assert in the recipe test that the focus-visible ring's resolved value is **not identical to the default state** — an invisible focus state is a WCAG 2.4.7 failure and is the exact bug `zimmButton.css.ts` records having already shipped once. Figma supplies no hover/focus node for the stepper; inheritance is the resolution, annotated at the point of use. Do not invent a value.
6. Each button has an `aria-label` (`IconButton` renders no visible text — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`).
7. Resolved target size of each control is ≥24×24 CSS px, asserted from the recipe, not measured in a browser.
8. `index.stories.tsx` has a `play` covering increment, decrement, and the disabled-at-1 boundary.

#### Step 3.2 — `ZimmInlineMessage` atom + error/warning states

**Changes.** New atom, variant-driven: `error` (`status.error`) / `warning` (`text.muted`). It sits **between the stepper and the actions row**, full width, `textStyle="caption"` with weight overridden to regular per gate #13. In error states the Item Details gap widens 12 → 16px — that is a recipe state on `ZimmCartItem`, not a prop on the message.

**Presentation only.** OOS / partial OOS triggering is SFCC-282 and Unavailable is SFCC-796 — both Sprint 6, Hazel's. Build prop-driven with stories; do not wire detection logic.

Copy, verbatim from Figma: fully OOS **"This item is unavailable"**; partial OOS **"Quantity unavailable in this size"**; max quantity **"Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size"**.

Per gate #4, max-quantity renders as the **warning** variant (grey, `text.muted`), not error — the design and SFCC-250 AC4 agree; CAI-017's word "error" means user-facing feedback, not the severity tier. Annotate that reconciliation inline.

Per gate #9, **there is no low-stock variant** — CAI-030 forbids low-stock messaging at cart level. Do not add one.

**Pass criteria.**
1. Stories: `Error`, `Warning`, plus one per copy string above. Each renders the exact copy.
2. `error` resolves to `var(--zimm-color-status-error)`; `warning` to `var(--zimm-color-text-muted)`. Both asserted in the recipe test against the token var, not a hex.
3. The organism recipe test asserts Item Details gap is the 12px token by default and the 16px token in the error state.
4. Message renders in DOM order **between** stepper and actions.
5. No `#9c0000`, `#969696` or any hex literal in either file — `npm run audit:tokens` clean.
6. No low-stock variant exists in the component's variant union.

#### Step 3.3 — Promotional price + discount label

**Changes.** The was/now mechanism **already exists** in base `display-price` (`priceData` with `listPrice`/`currentPrice`/`isOnSale`, renders `ListPrice` struck, already multiplies by quantity so it is line-item aware). Only the **discount label** ("20% off applied") is new, and it is purely presentational — prop-driven, storied, wired when the promotions engine lands. It renders beneath the stepper.

`display-price` has **no override** and is a shared SFCC internal. Do not override it in this step; if Zimmermann styling is needed later it goes through the bridge pattern (faithful default export, styling in a recipe).

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## Usage notes

- Always include a short description summarizing what the agent will do
- When the agent is done, its final report is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Trust but verify: an agent's summary describes what it intended to do, not necessarily what it did. When an agent writes or edits code, check the actual changes before reporting the work as done.
- To continue a previously spawned agent, use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name as the `to` field — that resumes it with full context. A new Agent call starts a fresh agent with no memory of prior runs (except subagent_type: "fork"), so the prompt must be self-contained.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a given bash command and returns its output.

The working directory persists between commands, but shell state does not. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh).

IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user:

 - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
 - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
 - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
While the Bash tool can do similar things, it’s better to use the built-in tools as they provide a better user experience and make it easier to review tool calls and give permission.

# Instructions
 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each stdout line is a notification). For one-shot "wait until done," use Bash with run_in_background instead.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - Long leading `sleep` commands are blocked. To poll until a condition is met, use Monitor with an until-loop (e.g. `until <check>; do sleep 2; done`) — you get a notification when the loop exits. Do not chain shorter sleeps to work around the block.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
- When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + tab. Everything after that is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the old_string or new_string.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
- Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}) as your last tool call and then stop. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your turn is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

1	import React, { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
2	import type { RefObject } from 'react';
3	import { useDisclosure } from '@chakra-ui/react';
4	import { useLocation } from 'react-router-dom';
5	import logger from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/logger-instance';
6	import { CartDrawerContainer } from 'app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer';
7	
8	/*
9	 * SFCC-11 plan step 9 (final commit) — mirrors the shape of base's own
10	 * `use-add-to-cart-modal.js` (a state-builder hook + a Context Provider + a Context-reading
11	 * hook), but simpler in one real, verified way: unlike base's modal, this drawer takes no
12	 * "item added" payload at all — across all 17 Figma state groups there is no "just added" state,
13	 * the drawer always renders whatever the current basket contains (see `CartDrawerContainer`'s own
14	 * docblock). So the shared state here is just isOpen/onOpen/onClose, and Chakra's own
15	 * `useDisclosure()` — already used for exactly this shape elsewhere in this codebase
16	 * (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:126`) — is the more idiomatic choice than hand-rolling base's raw
17	 * `useState`.
18	 *
19	 * Two real constraints shaped this file, both found by reading the actual current code rather
20	 * than assumed:
21	 *
22	 * 1. **The structural trap base's own code fell into.** `AddToCartModalProvider` is mounted in
23	 *    base `_app` today, but `<AddToCartModal />` itself is never rendered anywhere, base or
24	 *    override (confirmed by grepping the whole `retail-react-app` package) — a component can't
25	 *    easily be both a Context's wrapper and a Context's consumer of its own child in the same
26	 *    render pass, and base's own code never solved that, so add-to-cart has shipped with zero
27	 *    visual feedback. Fixed here by making `CartDrawerProvider` itself render
28	 *    `CartDrawerContainer` (the file that actually renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>` with real basket
29	 *    content) — the Provider can never be mounted without the real UI being fed real props,
30	 *    because both happen in the same component body.
31	 *
32	 * 2. **`_app` needs this same live state for its own bag-icon click handler, and `_app` is the
33	 *    component that mounts `CartDrawerProvider`.** A component cannot consume a context it is
34	 *    itself providing within its own subtree — there is no ancestor `CartDrawerProvider` above
35	 *    `_app`'s own top-level code, only a descendant one it's about to render. `useCartDrawerState`
36	 *    is exported separately from `useCartDrawer` so `_app` can call the *raw* state builder
37	 *    directly (the same way it already calls plain `useDisclosure()` directly for its own mobile
38	 *    nav drawer state) and pass the resulting value into `<CartDrawerProvider value={...}>` —
39	 *    so `_app`'s own handler and every nested consumer (`product-view`) always observe the
40	 *    identical live state, never two independent copies. `useCartDrawer()` (the Context reader)
41	 *    is for every other consumer, which — unlike `_app` — genuinely is a descendant of the
42	 *    Provider.
43	 */
44	
45	export type CartDrawerContextValue = {
46	  /** Whether the drawer is open. */
47	  isOpen: boolean;
48	  /**
49	   * Opens the drawer. Pass the element that should receive focus back once the drawer closes
50	   * (AC10) — e.g. the real clicked `<button>`/`<IconButton>` DOM node. Mirrors
51	   * `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `handleTriggerClick` (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:267-276`):
52	   * capture a real element at the moment of the triggering interaction, rather than reading
53	   * `document.activeElement` later — that file's own comment on why
54	   * (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:268-269`) applies identically here: a mouse click does not
55	   * reliably focus the clicked element in every browser. Omit/pass `null`/`undefined` when no
56	   * trigger element is available; the previous trigger (if any) is left untouched rather than
57	   * cleared, so a best-effort focus target is still preferred over none.
58	   */
59	  onOpen: (trigger?: HTMLElement | null) => void;
60	  /** Closes the drawer. Does not clear `triggerRef` — see `handleCloseComplete` in
61	   *  `zimmDrawer/index.tsx`, which reads `finalFocusRef` only after the close animation
62	   *  finishes, i.e. strictly after `onClose` has already run. Clearing the ref here would
63	   *  make AC10 focus-return silently fail on every close. */
64	  onClose: () => void;
65	  /** AC10 focus-return target — whichever element was last passed to `onOpen`. Forward to
66	   *  `ZimmDrawer`/`CartDrawerContainer`'s `finalFocusRef` prop. Typed as `RefObject<HTMLElement>`
67	   *  (not `| null`) to satisfy that prop's own type — same typing precedent as
68	   *  `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `triggerRef` (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:88,140`). */
69	  triggerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement>;
70	};
71	
72	// Exported (not just used internally) for the same reason base exports `AddToCartModalContext`
73	// directly (`use-add-to-cart-modal.js:59`) — lets a test wrap a subtree with a controlled value
74	// via `CartDrawerContext.Provider` directly, without going through the real state builder.
75	export const CartDrawerContext = createContext<CartDrawerContextValue | undefined>(undefined);
76	
77	/**
78	 * Builds the cart drawer's shared isOpen/onOpen/onClose state plus its AC10 focus-return
79	 * trigger ref — the raw equivalent of base's own `useAddToCartModal()`. Called exactly once, by
80	 * `_app`, which passes the result into `CartDrawerProvider`'s `value` prop — see this file's own
81	 * module docblock (constraint 2) for why `_app` needs the raw builder rather than
82	 * `useCartDrawer()`'s Context read.
83	 *
84	 * @returns The shared cart-drawer state — see `CartDrawerContextValue`.
85	 */
86	export const useCartDrawerState = (): CartDrawerContextValue => {
87	  const { isOpen, onOpen: onDisclosureOpen, onClose } = useDisclosure();
88	  // Typed as HTMLElement (not HTMLElement | null) so `.current` is writable below — same cast
89	  // and reasoning as useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:140 (a plain `useRef<HTMLElement>(null)` would
90	  // infer the read-only `RefObject<HTMLElement>` overload instead of `MutableRefObject`).
91	  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null as unknown as HTMLElement);
92	
93	  const onOpen = (trigger?: HTMLElement | null): void => {
94	    if (trigger) triggerRef.current = trigger;
95	    onDisclosureOpen();
96	  };
97	
98	  // Judgement call (no AC or Figma state describes this either way — see this hook's own
99	  // module docblock and the PR report for the fuller reasoning): close the drawer whenever the
100	  // route changes, mirroring base `use-add-to-cart-modal.js`'s own `[pathname]`-keyed effect
101	  // (`use-add-to-cart-modal.js:603-611`) and this exact file's sibling precedent —
102	  // `_app/index.tsx`'s own mobile-nav drawer already closes itself the same way
103	  // (`_app/index.tsx`'s own `useEffect(() => { onClose(); }, [location])`, "Lets automatically
104	  // close the mobile navigation when the location path is changed."). Concretely load-bearing,
105	  // not just consistency: `ZimmCartButtonGroup`'s Checkout button (already built, SFCC-275)
106	  // navigates via a plain `history.push('/checkout')` with no `onClose` call of its own
107	  // (verified directly against `zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx`'s `handleCheckoutClick`), and
108	  // `ZimmDrawer`'s overlay is not click-through — without this effect, clicking Checkout from
109	  // inside the cart drawer would navigate to `/checkout` while the drawer stayed open on top of
110	  // it, leaving the shopper unable to see or reach the page they just navigated to.
111	  const { pathname } = useLocation();
112	  useEffect(() => {
113	    if (isOpen) {
114	      onClose();
115	    }
116	    // Deliberately keyed on pathname alone, matching use-add-to-cart-modal.js's own shape —
117	    // isOpen/onClose are read for their current value, not to decide when the effect re-runs.
118	  }, [pathname]);
119	
120	  return { isOpen, onOpen, onClose, triggerRef };
121	};
122	
123	// Stable (module-level, not per-render) no-op fallback for when no CartDrawerProvider is
124	// mounted above the caller — see useCartDrawer's own doc for why this degrades instead of
125	// throwing. `triggerRef` is a plain inert object, not a real useRef() result: nothing outside a
126	// real CartDrawerProvider subtree ever reads it back for a real focus call.
127	const FALLBACK_ONLY: CartDrawerContextValue = {
128	  isOpen: false,
129	  onOpen: () => {
130	    // A real shopper's page always has a CartDrawerProvider ancestor (mounted once in `_app`),
131	    // so reaching this in a real request is a genuine bug, not an expected path — logged so a
132	    // silently-broken Add to Bag button is at least observable, rather than a shopper clicking
133	    // it and nothing happening with no trace anywhere.
134	    logger.warn('useCartDrawer called with no CartDrawerProvider mounted — Add to Bag will not open the cart drawer.', {
135	      namespace: 'useCartDrawer',
136	    });
137	  },
138	  onClose: () => undefined,
139	  triggerRef: { current: null },
140	};
141	
142	/**
143	 * Reads the shared cart-drawer state from Context. For any consumer that is a genuine descendant
144	 * of `CartDrawerProvider` (e.g. `product-view`) — see this file's own module docblock for why
145	 * `_app` itself must use `useCartDrawerState()` directly instead.
146	 *
147	 * Degrades to a stable, harmless no-op outside a Provider — the same shape `useUiCopy.ts` already
148	 * uses (`useContext(...) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`) — rather than throwing. Confirmed necessary, not
149	 * merely convenient: `product-view/index.stories.tsx` (unmodified by this change — not in this
150	 * step's own manifest) wraps `ProductView`'s stories in the now-removed `AddToCartModalProvider`,
151	 * with no `CartDrawerProvider` in its own decorator stack, and every one of its stories renders
152	 * the real default `ProductView` export, which calls this hook unconditionally near its own top
153	 * level. A throwing `useCartDrawer` (this file's own first draft, matching `useIntl`'s
154	 * load-bearing/non-degrading precedent) crashes all four of that file's stories on mount, before
155	 * any interaction — verified live against a real running Storybook instance, not assumed (see
156	 * this step's own PR report). `onOpen`'s own no-op additionally logs a warning (see
157	 * `FALLBACK_ONLY` above) so a genuine missing-Provider bug in the real app — which should never
158	 * happen, since `_app` always mounts one — is still observable rather than a silent dead button.
159	 *
160	 * @returns The shared cart-drawer state — see `CartDrawerContextValue`.
161	 */
162	export const useCartDrawer = (): CartDrawerContextValue => useContext(CartDrawerContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;
163	
164	export type CartDrawerProviderProps = {
165	  /** The live state to provide — built via `useCartDrawerState()` by the one caller (`_app`)
166	   *  that also needs it directly for its own bag-icon click handler. Accepting it as a prop
167	   *  (rather than calling `useCartDrawerState()` internally) is what lets `_app` and every
168	   *  nested consumer share the exact same instance — see this file's own module docblock,
169	   *  constraint 2. */
170	  value: CartDrawerContextValue;
171	  children: React.ReactNode;
172	};
173	
174	/**
175	 * Provides the shared cart-drawer state to `children` AND renders `CartDrawerContainer` — the
176	 * component that actually renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>` with real basket content — in the same
177	 * place. See this file's own module docblock, constraint 1, for why both happen together here
178	 * rather than leaving `CartDrawerContainer` for some other, easily-forgotten call site to mount.
179	 *
180	 * Written with `React.createElement` rather than JSX so this file can stay `.ts` (as named in
181	 * the SFCC-11 plan's own file manifest) — every other source file under `overrides/app/hooks/`
182	 * is `.ts` with no JSX in it; `useUiCopy.ts`'s own Provider is a separate `.tsx` component under
183	 * `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/` rather than living in the hook file itself, which
184	 * is the established split this codebase already uses for exactly this shape. Splitting
185	 * `CartDrawerProvider` out the same way was the more consistent option but would have meant
186	 * creating a file outside this step's own manifest — flagged in the PR report, not decided
187	 * silently. `React.createElement(...)` has one direct precedent already in this codebase for
188	 * the identical reason (a `.ts` file needing to produce a React element without JSX syntax):
189	 * `overrides/app/components/forms/useAddressFields.test.ts:26`.
190	 */
191	export const CartDrawerProvider = ({ value, children }: CartDrawerProviderProps): React.ReactElement =>
192	  React.createElement(
193	    CartDrawerContext.Provider,
194	    { value },
195	    children,
196	    React.createElement(CartDrawerContainer, {
197	      isOpen: value.isOpen,
198	      onClose: value.onClose,
199	      finalFocusRef: value.triggerRef,
200	    }),
201	  );
202

19	import {useIntl} from 'react-intl'
20	
21	/**
22	 * A Modal that contains Product View
23	 */
24	const ProductViewModal = ({product, isOpen, onClose, ...props}) => {
25	    const productViewModalData = useProductViewModal(product)
26	
27	    const intl = useIntl()
28	    const label = intl.formatMessage(
29	        {
30	            defaultMessage: 'Edit modal for {productName}',
31	            id: 'cart.product_edit_modal.modal_label'
32	        },
33	        {productName: productViewModalData?.product?.name}
34	    )
35	
36	    return (
37	        <Modal size="4xl" isOpen={isOpen} onClose={onClose}>
38	            <ModalOverlay />
39	            <ModalContent containerProps={{'data-testid': 'product-view-modal'}} aria-label={label}>
40	                <ModalCloseButton />
41	                <ModalBody pb={8} bg="white" paddingBottom={6} marginTop={6}>
42	                    <ProductView
43	                        showFullLink={true}
44	                        imageSize="sm"
45	                        product={productViewModalData.product}
46	                        isLoading={productViewModalData.isFetching}
47	                        {...props}
48	                    />
49	                </ModalBody>
50	            </ModalContent>
51	        </Modal>
52	    )
53	}
54	
55	ProductViewModal.propTypes = {
56	    isOpen: PropTypes.bool.isRequired,
57	    onOpen: PropTypes.func.isRequired,
58	    onClose: PropTypes.func.isRequired,
59	    product: PropTypes.object,
60	    isLoading: PropTypes.bool
61	}
62	
63	export default ProductViewModal

input.message:
Scope covered: AC-by-AC verification against plan.md §9 "B1 — pass criteria" items 2-4, 6-11 (item 1 skipped per assignment, item 5 skipped per assignment), plus the full point-12 regression investigation. Working tree diff reviewed (`git diff` on the 4 modified files + read of the 2 new `useCartDrawer.*` files); nothing else in the repo was touched — confirmed via `git status --short` before and after, identical to the session's starting snapshot.

## Item 2 — Bag icon opens drawer, does not navigate
`overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx:332-333`. CONFIRMED, 🔵, UNIFORM. `onCartClick` no longer contains `history.push`/`buildUrl('/cart')` — body is now `cartDrawer.onOpen(e?.currentTarget ?? null); onClose();` (the `onClose` is the pre-existing, unrelated mobile-nav-drawer close). Repo-wide grep (`grep -rn "buildUrl('/cart')" overrides/`) returns zero hits — no other call site resurrects cart navigation.

## Item 3 — Add-to-bag opens drawer, not base AddToCartModal
`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:453`. CONFIRMED, 🔵, UNIFORM. `useAddToCartModalContext` import is gone; `useCartDrawer()` destructure replaces it. Repo-wide grep for `useAddToCartModalContext|onAddToCartModalOpen|AddToCartModalProvider` under `overrides/` returns **zero** matches in functional code — only in comments/docblocks that reference the removal, and one pre-existing file not touched by this diff: `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.stories.tsx:26,70` still imports/wraps stories in the base `AddToCartModalProvider`. This is dead (no-op) wrapping now, not a broken call site — `useCartDrawer.ts`'s own module docblock (lines 149-158) already discloses this exact gap and explains why `useCartDrawer()` degrades via `FALLBACK_ONLY` instead of throwing, specifically because this stories file (out of this step's manifest) has no `CartDrawerProvider` in its decorator stack. 🔵 ONE-OFF, informational, already disclosed — not a new finding.

## Item 4 — no "item added" payload, ever
CONFIRMED, 🔵, UNIFORM. Every call site checked:
- `_app/index.tsx:333` — `cartDrawer.onOpen(e?.currentTarget ?? null)`
- `product-view/index.tsx:620` — `onCartDrawerOpen(trigger)` where `trigger = addToBagTriggerRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('button')`
- `product-view/index.tsx:906` — `onCartDrawerOpen(e?.currentTarget ?? null)`

All three pass only a DOM element (or null) as the sole optional argument. `useCartDrawer.ts`'s own type signature structurally enforces this: `onOpen: (trigger?: HTMLElement | null) => void` — there is no second parameter to smuggle a payload through. `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (already committed, step 4.6) independently confirms the architecture: it takes only `isOpen`/`onClose`/`finalFocusRef` and derives all content from its own `useCurrentBasket()` call, never from anything passed at open-time.

## Items 6-11 — pre-existing behaviour undisturbed
Full-repo `git status --short` / `git diff --stat` for this step touches exactly 4 files (`_app/index.tsx`, `_app/index.test.tsx`, `product-view/index.tsx`, `product-view/index.test.tsx`) plus 2 new files (`useCartDrawer.ts`, `.test.tsx`). Nothing else changed.
- **Item 6 (AC8 scroll/state on close):** zero diff to `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/` or `.../organisms/zimmCartDrawer/`. Undisturbed.
- **Items 7-9 (messages band height, panel widths, header count text):** zero diff to `zimmCartDrawer.css.ts` / `zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx` (neither appears in the changed-file list at all). Undisturbed.
- **Items 10-11 (live item count while open; nested wishlist-drawer scroll lock):** zero diff to `zimmDrawer/index.tsx` (owns `scrollLockCount`) or to basket-count rendering. Undisturbed.

## Item 12 — regression check (main deliverable)

**1. ccExtensibility config — CONFIRMED.** `package.json:17-20`:
```json
"ccExtensibility": {
  "extends": "@salesforce/retail-react-app",
  "overridesDir": "overrides"
}
```
This is the standard PWA Kit webpack-plugin override resolver — it redirects any import of `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view` (including from base's own `node_modules` files) to `overrides/app/components/product-view` in the real app build. Both candidate surfaces import that exact base specifier: `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view-modal/index.jsx:17` and `.../bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx:22`.

**2. Prop-surface compatibility — CONFIRMED.** `ProductView` stays `forwardRef`-wrapped (`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:379`, `forwardRef(`) with a plain `export default ProductView;` at line 1688 — unchanged shape. The diff's hunks touch only lines ~446-462 (hook swap), ~547-565 (new ref), ~602-622, ~863-918, ~990-1005, ~1298-1320 — nowhere near the `ProductViewProps` type block (~200-210), so the prop surface (`addToCart`, `showFullLink`, `imageSize`, `showImageGallery`, `isProductLoading`, `customButtons`, `promotionId`, `maxOrderQuantity`, `showReviews`, `showVariationAttributes`, `alignItems`, `imageGalleryFooter`, `controlledVariationValues`, `onVariationChange`, etc. — the full set both base modals pass) is untouched. Neither modal's own `<ProductView ...>` usage (`product-view-modal/index.jsx:42-48`, `bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx:464-482`) references anything this diff added/removed/renamed.

**3. Actual render attempt — got a real pass/fail on BOTH candidate surfaces, not just structural inference.**

Built a throwaway Vitest harness in the scratchpad (not the repo) to actually execute this. Two real obstacles, both solved:
- Vitest's own `vitest.config.ts` scopes `include` to `overrides/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, so a scratchpad file is invisible to it — wrote a standalone scratch config instead.
- Vite's resolver, for any importer physically outside the repo tree, does **not** fall back to a `root` option's `node_modules` for bare-specifier resolution (confirmed empirically: `react`, `vitest`, `@testing-library/react`, every `@salesforce/...` specifier all failed to resolve from a file under `/private/tmp/...`, even with `root` pointed at the repo). Fixed with a plain `node_modules` symlink placed inside the scratchpad, pointing at the repo's real `node_modules` — a filesystem-only fix, nothing in the repo touched.

With that working, built the same ~25-mock recipe the real, already-committed `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.test.tsx` uses to render `ProductView` cleanly, added `vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view', async () => await import('app/components/product-view'))` (this one line does exactly what the real webpack resolver does), and rendered the **base, unoverridden** `product-view-modal` straight from `node_modules`.

**Result — `product-view-modal`: 3/3 tests passed.**
- Base modal renders our override's real markup inside it (not blank, not crashed).
- Clicking the real Add to Bag button reaches `useCartDrawer().onOpen`, called with the exact clicked button element as trigger.
- When `addToCart` resolves with no items added, `onOpen` is correctly NOT called.

**Mutation check (not just a pass — proved the pass is meaningful).** Built a second variant that uses `importOriginal()` to load the REAL base `product-view.jsx` instead of our override (simulating "what if the ccExtensibility swap were missing"). It fails hard — base `product-view.jsx` pulls in base's `use-add-to-cart-modal.js`, which is JSX-in-a-`.js` file that Vitest's transform cannot parse (`Failed to parse source for import analysis... contains invalid JS syntax`). This confirms the original pass was load-bearing on the redirect actually being in effect, not vacuous — and independently corroborates (via a completely different code path) the same JSX-in-`.js` Vitest gap `testing.md` already documents for `use-auth-modal.js`.

**Then attempted the second surface too (`bonus-product-view-modal`) — also got a real result, plus a genuinely useful structural finding along the way.** Reading `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx:137-197` before building the harness surfaced this: its own custom `handleAddToCart` (passed as the `addToCart` prop to `<ProductView>`) **returns `null` on every single code path** — `productItems.length===0`, both success branches, and the catch block — with the success branches' own comment literally reading `// Return null to prevent AddToCartModal from opening`. Base itself deliberately built this modal to never trigger the shared add-to-cart-modal feedback path; it shows its own toast + navigates to `/cart` instead. Since our override's gate (`if (itemsAdded) { onCartDrawerOpen(...) }`) is the same shape as base's own (`if (itemsAdded) { onAddToCartModalOpen(...) }`), `itemsAdded` was **already** going to be falsy here in base, before this diff existed — this surface was never wired to the shared feedback path, in base or override. Not a regression; a pre-existing, deliberate base design choice that our change doesn't disturb.

Built the full harness anyway to confirm this empirically rather than leave it as a source-reading claim (needed ~9 more mocks: `useControlledVariations`, `useShopperBasketsV2MutationHelper`, `useCurrentBasket`, `useNavigation`, `useBonusProductCounts`, `checkForRemainingBonusProducts`, `processProductsForBonusCart`, and both `*ViewModalTheme` objects). **Result: 2/2 tests passed** — renders without crashing; clicking Add to Bag does not open the cart drawer. Added one extra assertion (`processProductsForBonusCart` was actually called) specifically to rule out a vacuous "never called" from a click that silently didn't fire — confirmed the click genuinely propagated through the real, unmocked `handleAddToBag`/`handleCartItem` → `addToCart(...)` chain.

**Verdict for item 12: CONFIRMED (not merely PLAUSIBLE) for both named surfaces**, 🔵, UNIFORM — via actual rendering + real click simulation, not structural inference alone:
- `product-view-modal` (the "quick-view"/edit modal): add-to-bag feedback is genuinely wired through to the cart drawer, mutation-verified.
- `bonus-product-view-modal`: correctly does **not** reach the cart drawer, but this is pre-existing base behaviour this diff neither created nor could have regressed (base's own code was already null-gated before SFCC-11).

Cleanup confirmed: all scratch files (`tester6-modalregr*.{ts,tsx}`, `tester6-bonusmodal.*`) and the `node_modules` symlink deleted; `ls` of the scratchpad shows none remain. `git status --short` in the repo is byte-identical to the pre-investigation snapshot — no repo file was created, modified, or deleted during this investigation.

This confirms the original pass was load-bearing on the redirect actually being in effect, not vacuous — and independently corroborates (via a completely different code path) the same JSX-in-`.js` Vitest gap `testing.md` already documents for `use-auth-modal.js`.

**Then attempted the second surface too (`bonus-product-view-modal`) — also got a real result, plus a genuinely useful structural finding along the way.** Reading `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx:137-197` before building the harness surfaced this: its own custom `handleAddToCart` (passed as the `addToCart` prop to `<ProductView>`) **returns `null` on every single code path** — `productItems.length===0`, both success branches, and the catch block — with the success branches' own comment literally reading `// Return null to prevent AddToCartModal from opening`. Base itself deliberately built this modal to never trigger the shared add-to-cart-modal feedback path; it shows its own toast + navigates to `/cart` instead. Since our override's gate (`if (itemsAdded) { onCartDrawerOpen(...) }`) is the same shape as base's own (`if (itemsAdded) { onAddToCartModalOpen(...) }`), `itemsAdded` was **already** going to be falsy here in base, before this diff existed — this surface was never wired to the shared feedback path, in base or override. Not a regression; a pre-existing, deliberate base design choice that our change doesn't disturb.

Built the full harness anyway to confirm this empirically rather than leave it as a source-reading claim (needed ~9 more mocks: `useControlledVariations`, `useShopperBasketsV2MutationHelper`, `useCurrentBasket`, `useNavigation`, `useBonusProductCounts`, `checkForRemainingBonusProducts`, `processProductsForBonusCart`, and both `*ViewModalTheme` objects). **Result: 2/2 tests passed** — renders without crashing; clicking Add to Bag does not open the cart drawer.
